newsitem.title: NORWAY: Analysts downbeat on possible Saga/Santa Fe deal.
newsitem.headline: Analysts downbeat on possible Saga/Santa Fe deal.

text.p: Shares in Norwegian oil company Saga Petroleum ASA are likely to tumble if speculation proves correct that the company will buy Sante Fe Exploration for $1.2 billion, a Reuter survey of five Norwegian and international analysts showed.
Saga shares were suspended on Monday pending an announcement on the takeover at 105.50 crowns.
The analysts attributed scepticism to the deal to the seemingly high price for the North Sea exploration company.
Saga is expected to announce imminently that it will buy Santa Fe from state-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC). Market speculation has pegged the price of the deal at $1.2 billion.
Analysts place Santa Fe's value closer to $700-800 million and say they expect the high premium paid by Saga will slash up to 20 percent off Saga's share price.
"Saga will have to work hard to justify the price," said one analyst. "I expect the share price to be cut by about 20 crowns."
"It was the most intensive auction in this sector that I've ever seen, the whole industry was bidding," the analyst said.
Nick Antill at London broker BZW estimated the discounted value of Santa Fe's reserves at about $700 million. Others put the British-based explorer between $700 and $750 million.
"It (the price rumoured for Saga) is very bullish," said Gundi Royle at Morgan Stanley, adding that even $1 billion would be exceptional.
SBC Warburg recently downgraded its recommendation on Saga to a sell and said the share price could possibly fall by 10 percent following the deal.
Only one of the analysts was positive to the takeover.
"People are turning their noses up to the deal, but that's premature," said the positive analyst. "Now Saga's opinion should be heard."
